title: How to Use ChatGPT or Claude to Write Your Resume
summary: Use five resume prompts in ChatGPT or Claude for bullets, summaries, skills and job tailoring, with a worked example and a review checklist.
body_markdown:
A good resume is like a good online dating profile: rarer than any of us would like. Synthesizing all your best skills and most attractive features as an employee into a short, well-written document is challenging for even the most practiced job applicants. That’s where an AI assistant such as[ChatGPT](https://openai.com/blog/chatgpt?ref=blog.simplify.jobs) or[Claude](https://claude.ai/?ref=blog.simplify.jobs) can help.


💡


Keep reading for our tips on using ChatGPT or Claude for your resume, including prompts to try and issues to watch out for!


## Resume prompts for ChatGPT and Claude


You can use ChatGPT or Claude to organize your experience, tailor it to a job, or improve one section at a time. Give your chosen assistant the facts first. Review the result before you put it on a resume.


The five main prompts below cover a first draft, job tailoring, experience bullets, a summary, and skills. Replace the bracketed instructions with your own material. You can use one prompt on its own; you do not have to run the whole sequence. Three short follow-ups after the templates help you uncover details, fix generic wording, and check the finished draft.


[OpenAI's official prompting guide](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/prompting?ref=blog.simplify.jobs) recommends explaining the task, relevant context, desired output, and boundaries. For a resume, one important boundary is that editing must not change what you actually did.


## How to use these prompts in ChatGPT or Claude


Choose the tool you already use and paste the relevant materials with one prompt. These templates ask for ordinary text editing and comparison; they do not depend on a particular model name, file-upload feature, or special syntax.


[Claude's official prompting guidance](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/claude-prompting-best-practices?ref=blog.simplify.jobs) also recommends explicit instructions, relevant context, and examples of the result you want.


- Start with one task, such as rewriting selected bullets, rather than requesting a full resume overhaul at once.
- Keep follow-up edits in the same conversation so the materials and corrections remain together. Ask for one specific change at a time.
- Judge the result against your source facts. If you try both tools, give each the same materials and instructions, then compare accuracy, relevance, and the amount of editing needed.


A more polished sentence is only useful if it remains true. This guide does not rank ChatGPT against Claude or claim that either produces more interviews.


## What to give the AI before you ask it to write


Prepare a small set of source materials:


- **Your current resume or factual notes:** roles, dates, education, projects, and responsibilities.
- **The target job description:** paste the relevant text so you can check exactly what the prompt is using.
- **Evidence for your achievements:** tools used, your contribution, deliverables, and any results you can verify.
- **The section you want to work on:** a full outline, selected bullets, a summary, or a skills list.
- **Details that must stay unchanged:** official titles, employers, dates, qualifications, and the scope of your responsibility.


Remove contact details, references' information, and confidential employer or customer data before sharing your material. Replace identifying details with labels where possible. You can put the necessary contact information back into the final document yourself.


Keep an unchanged copy of your original resume. It gives you a reference when a rewrite sounds stronger than the evidence behind it.


## 1. Build a resume draft from your experience


Use this when you have notes but no organized resume. Include class projects, campus activities, volunteering, or part-time work if they provide relevant evidence. Do not turn them into paid positions or inflate your role.


**Paste:** your factual notes and the target job description.


```text
Help me organize a resume for the target role below using only my notes.


If missing or conflicting facts prevent an accurate draft, ask up to
five specific questions and wait for my answers. Otherwise, proceed
without a question round. Do not invent an employer, title, date,
qualification, skill, responsibility, or result. The job description
guides relevance; it is not evidence of my experience.


Suggest a section order, then draft the most relevant experience or
project section in plain text. Keep official job titles unchanged and
make my personal contribution clear. Leave out unsupported claims.
List unresolved details separately from the draft. Work on the
remaining sections one at a time after I review this section.


Target role and job description:
[Paste here]


My experience, education, projects, and verified achievements:
[Paste here]
```


Check whether the draft distinguishes what you did from what your team did. If you helped test a feature, the bullet should say that. It should not quietly become ownership of the feature's design or launch.


## 2. Tailor your resume to a job description


Tailoring means selecting and emphasizing relevant experience. Your history stays the same. Start with a comparison before asking for a rewrite so you can see which requirements your evidence actually supports.


**Paste:** the job description and your current resume.


```text
Compare my resume with the job description below.


Return a table quoting each relevant job requirement and the exact
supporting text from my resume, with a status: supported, partly
supported, or not shown. Start with explicitly required qualifications
and core responsibilities. Do not invent the employer's priorities or
treat a requirement as proof that I have it.


Then suggest up to five edits that make my relevant experience easier to
find. Name the section to edit and show the original and proposed
wording for each. Preserve titles, dates, tools, numbers, and level of
responsibility. Ask about missing evidence instead of adding it.


Job description:
[Paste here]


Current resume:
[Paste here]
```


Review the comparison before accepting the edits. If the posting asks for SQL and your resume only shows spreadsheet work, SQL belongs in the gap column until you can provide real experience with it. Our[resume skill keywords guide](https://simplify.jobs/blog/most-important-skill-keywords-for-resume?ref=blog.simplify.jobs) explains how to make these choices without copying every requirement.


## 3. Rewrite experience bullets with clearer evidence


A useful bullet tells the reader what you did and why it mattered. A number can help when it is real, but a clear deliverable, scale, or decision is useful too.


**Paste:** the original bullets, supporting facts, and any relevant job requirements.


```text
Rewrite the bullets below so they clearly explain my action, the work or
tool involved, and the supported result or deliverable.


Use only my original bullets and verified supporting facts as evidence.
Use job requirements only to decide what is relevant. Preserve my level
of responsibility and any verified numbers I supply. Do not introduce,
estimate, or calculate a new metric. Ask about a missing detail rather
than filling it in; a concrete deliverable is enough without a metric.


First return the revised bullets alone, ready to paste into a resume.
Aim for about 20-30 words each, but keep necessary facts even if a
bullet needs more space. Then show each original, its revision, and the
exact source facts used. Flag wording that could overstate my contribution.


Original bullets:
[Paste here]


Verified supporting facts about my work:
[Paste here]


Relevant job requirements (context only, not facts about me):
[Paste here]
```


The word range is an editing target you can adjust, not a hiring rule. Keep the evidence and your actual contribution clear before trimming for length.


### Worked example: from a vague bullet to a defensible one


**This is a fictional teaching example, not a real candidate's result or a recorded test of either tool.** The following materials and edits are written to show what to check.


**Target role:** entry-level data analyst. The job description asks for SQL, data cleaning, and clear communication.


**Original bullet:**


> Helped with reporting for the campus food pantry.


**Verified notes supplied with the prompt:**


- Volunteered at a campus food pantry.
- Used SQL to combine weekly inventory spreadsheets covering 12 weeks.
- Checked duplicate item records and missing category labels.
- Prepared a weekly stock summary for the volunteer coordinator.
- Did not measure time saved, cost savings, or the effect on food availability.


**An acceptable revision:**


> Combined 12 weeks of food-pantry inventory records with SQL, checked duplicates and missing categories, and prepared weekly stock summaries for the volunteer coordinator.


The revision names the tool, work, scope, and audience. Every claim comes from the notes. It does not need an invented percentage to be specific.


**An edit to reject:**


> Led a SQL analytics initiative that reduced food waste by 30% and saved 10 hours per week.


The notes do not support leadership, a reduction in waste, or time savings. Those additions would need to be removed, even if the sentence sounds impressive.


A useful follow-up question would be: "How did the coordinator use the stock summary?" If you can verify the answer, you may be able to describe the value more clearly. If you cannot, the deliverable is enough.


Turn your reviewed bullets into a resume you can edit and export.


[Build my resume](https://simplify.jobs/resume-builder?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=cta&utm_campaign=how-to-use-chatgpt-to-write-and-improve-your-resume&utm_content=worked-example-cta)


## 4. Draft a summary that fits your background


Use a summary when it adds context, such as explaining a career change or a relevant combination of experience. It is optional; our guide to[whether you need a resume summary](https://simplify.jobs/blog/do-you-need-a-resume-summary?ref=blog.simplify.jobs) covers that decision.


**Paste:** your verified background, target role, and, if available, the job description.


```text
Draft two resume summary options of no more than two sentences each for
the target role below.


Use only my verified background as evidence. If I include a job
description, use it to select relevant facts, not to add qualifications.
Give the options different, supported points of emphasis. If my facts
support only one useful version, return one and explain why.


Do not invent years of experience, certifications, achievements, or
seniority. Avoid generic labels such as "results-driven" and "dynamic."


Keep official job titles unchanged. If my background does not support a
useful summary, explain what is missing instead of padding it.


Return the summaries first, without review notes inside them. Below
each, name its emphasis and quote the source facts supporting it.


Target role:
[Paste here]


Job description (optional, for relevance only):
[Paste here or omit]


Verified background:
[Paste here]
```


Choose the version that helps a reader understand your fit. Remove any claim you would need to walk back in an interview. A student project can demonstrate experience using a tool without making you an experienced professional in that field.


## 5. Choose skills you can support


Give your chosen assistant both the job requirements and evidence of your skills. A keyword found in a posting is a requirement to evaluate, not automatically something to add to your resume.


**Paste:** the job description, your current skills list, and experience or project notes.


```text
Suggest a focused skills section for this job using only skills
supported by my materials.


First return a concise skills section I can paste into my resume.
Group the supported skills into readable categories. Keep evidence and
review notes outside this final section.


Then list each included skill with its exact supporting source text,
job requirements not shown in my materials, and specific questions
about unclear experience. Not shown does not mean I lack a skill;
ask me to confirm it before suggesting that I add it.


Do not add a tool because it is similar to one I used. Do not assign
proficiency levels or claim certifications I have not supplied. Treat
the job description as context, not proof of my skills. Suggest where
an experience or project bullet could demonstrate an important skill.


Job description:
[Paste here]


My current skills and supporting experience:
[Paste here]
```


Review the gap list as carefully as the proposed skills section. Remove anything you cannot explain through a project, class, or work example. Our guide to[how many skills to list](https://simplify.jobs/blog/how-many-skills-on-a-resume?ref=blog.simplify.jobs) can help you trim an overcrowded section.


## Three short follow-ups when the first draft needs work


Use these in the same conversation as the main prompt so the assistant has your original materials. If you start a new conversation, paste your source notes and the draft again. Choose the follow-up that fits the problem.


### Uncover details when your experience sounds thin


```text
Before rewriting, ask me one question at a time, up to five questions,
about the work's scope, frequency, deliverable, who used it, or what
changed. Do not suggest or estimate numbers. If I cannot verify an
outcome, help me describe the concrete work instead. Use only my
answers and original notes when we return to drafting.
```


### Replace generic wording with specific evidence


```text
Identify up to three phrases in this draft that could describe almost
any candidate. For each, quote the phrase and ask what specific fact
would make it useful. Wait for my answers before rewriting. Keep my
voice, level of responsibility, and verified facts unchanged; do not
replace vague language with unsupported claims.
```


### Check the draft against your original facts


```text
Compare this draft with my original notes. Check numbers, dates,
titles, tools, skills, credentials, and my level of responsibility.
Return a table with the claim, exact source text, and status: supported,
unclear, or unsupported. Put claims needing review first. Flag gaps for
me to confirm or remove; do not fill them in or silently rewrite them.
```


## Review the result before you use it


A prompt can tell either assistant to preserve facts, but you still need to check that it did. Compare each revision with your original material.


#### Final resume review checklist


- **Facts:** confirm employers, titles, dates, qualifications, and tools.
- **Numbers:** trace every count, percentage, time saving, or financial result to a source you can explain.
- **Ownership:** keep "assisted," "built," and "led" aligned with your actual contribution.
- **Relevance and voice:** remove unsupported keywords and sentences you would not naturally use.
- **The final file:** check the exported document for missing sections, awkward line breaks, and changed wording.


If a sentence is inaccurate, explain the specific issue in a follow-up. For example: "I helped test this feature but did not lead the project. Revise the bullet using that distinction and keep the verified facts unchanged." Asking for something "more impressive" gives you less control over what changes.


## Put the reviewed text into a usable resume


Once the wording is accurate, organize it in a resume you can edit, check, and export. In[Simplify Resume Builder](https://simplify.jobs/resume-builder?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=cta&utm_campaign=how-to-use-chatgpt-to-write-and-improve-your-resume&utm_content=body-1) , you can create or import a resume, keep editable versions, and compare keywords with a target job description. Building, scoring, keyword matching, and exporting are free; AI rewriting and job-specific AI tailoring are part of Simplify+.


A score is feedback to inspect, not a prediction that an employer will interview you. Review the issue details and read the final file yourself. The[Builder guide](https://help.simplify.jobs/en/articles/8040103-build-and-tailor-your-resume-on-simplify?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=cta&utm_campaign=how-to-use-chatgpt-to-write-and-improve-your-resume&utm_content=body-2) explains target jobs, versions, and how to review proposed changes.


## Common questions


### What is the best ChatGPT prompt for a resume?


Choose a prompt for the section or task you need. Include your factual background, the relevant job requirements, the output you want, and details that must stay unchanged. The five templates above are starting points, not a guarantee of a correct result.


### Can ChatGPT or Claude help if I have no work experience?


Either tool can help organize real projects, coursework, volunteering, and campus activities. Supply the details yourself and label each experience accurately. It should ask for missing facts rather than invent paid work or accomplishments.


### Can I use these ChatGPT resume prompts in Claude?


Yes. The prompts specify the task, source material, output, and factual limits without relying on a ChatGPT-only feature. Paste the same relevant materials into Claude and review its response against the same checklist. The results can differ, so do not assume either version is automatically correct.


### Can I paste the result directly into an application?


Review it first. Check each claim against your source material, edit wording that overstates your contribution, and inspect the final document. You are responsible for the version you submit.


Keep the right resume version for each job.
